Move the lock to `harness/.temper/lock.toml` so the fixture resolves `HarnessPath::Root` and the run gates the fixture. Then make the root decidable: build the case as `parent = common::tmpdir(...)`, `harness = parent.join("collision")`, plant a real `parent/.claude/rules/planted.md` beside it, and assert the run's `coverage.checked` note reports `rule (0)` — pre-fix it reports `rule (1)`, because the planted sibling sits at the root the run actually walked. The collision assertions (:272-290) are unchanged; the collision is a lock-declaration fact independent of the corpus, which is exactly why this rooting bug stayed invisible.

`tmpdir` (:31) persists every fixture with `.keep()` directly at /tmp's top level, so debris grows monotonically (9 GB / 37k entries swept by hand on 09-07) and any fixture that re-roots walks all of it. Give the suite ONE per-run parent under `tempfile` — a `Once`-initialized `/tmp/<fixed-prefix>-<rand>/` (`Once` is already imported at :16) that every `tmpdir` call nests under — so a sweep is one `rm -rf <prefix>-*` and a re-rooted run is bounded to that binary's own fixtures instead of the whole of /tmp. `.keep()` stays: the doc comment at :27 states the reason (callers hand paths across process boundaries that outlive the `TempDir` guard), so update that comment for the new parent rather than dropping it. The change is confined to this one function — all 323 `tmpdir(` call sites across tests/ take the returned `PathBuf` and none asserts on its path shape (verified by grep at scoping).

edit.description: `harness_diagnostics(&harness_path, &layers)?` (:240) aborts BEFORE the reporter match (:242-249), so a harness that fails to LOAD never reaches any reporter: miette renders the error to stderr and main exits non-zero with an empty stdout. For `--reporter session-start` that is the placement silently passing — Claude Code's SessionStart hook reads stdout JSON, so the session opens with no temper context and no verdict at all. Both `?` sites (`resolve_harness_path`, `gate::gate`) are inside `harness_diagnostics` (:704-713), so catching at this one call site covers every load fault. Catch the load error, lower it to one `error` Diagnostic, and run the SELECTED reporter over it. Terminal/GitHub/SARIF keep exiting non-zero (the exit rule is :261-262); session-start keeps its advisory exit 0 (the comment at :255 states why) but MUST print its payload.

The lowering helper's home — `Diagnostic` is defined here (:47), `Announcement` at :168 (it derives `Default`, so `Announcement::default()` is the constructor the reporter call needs). A `miette::Report` (the load failure) becomes one `error` Diagnostic. TWO mechanics the fix turns on, neither optional: (i) the `rule` is the report's own `miette::Diagnostic::code()` rendered to a string when it carries one, falling back to `gate.load-fault` when it does not — three existing tests assert the miette code deliberately (tests/toml_document.rs:249, tests/marketplace_kind.rs:195, tests/plugin_manifest_kind.rs:143), and `compose::IdentityMapError` declares no `#[diagnostic(code(...))]`, so the duplicate-key case lands on `gate.load-fault` exactly as this entry wants; (ii) the message renders the report's full `.chain()`, not bare `Display` — `TomlDocumentError::Io`/`NotUtf8` (src/toml_document.rs:104-123) carry their detail in a `#[source]` that `Display` alone drops, and seven modules use `#[source]`. Precedent to follow and to name in the commit body: `compose::frontmatter_fault_diagnostic` (:633-661) lowers three frontmatter faults to `member.load-fault` and re-raises the rest — say why the general helper lands here beside `Diagnostic` rather than beside that one. Do NOT assert a Claude Code hook-loading consequence in the message without a retrieved cite at the site (collaboration rule, external facts); the fact in `notes` is scoping rationale and must not migrate into shipped text.

VERIFY-ONLY — expect no diff here. `session_start` (:66) delegates to `context` (:94), which already renders every `Severity::Error` diagnostic into its Blocking findings block and already caps at `ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT_CAP` (:42) through `cap` (:172), on char boundaries. Confirm a single long miette message still caps cleanly; if it does, this file is untouched. It is inside the fence so the confirmation can be made, not because an edit is expected.

SECOND arm, and the only pin mechanic (ii) has anywhere: a `.claude/settings.json` that is not valid UTF-8 — `JsonManifestError::NotUtf8` (src/json_manifest.rs:253) carries its detail in a `#[source]` (:257) that bare `Display` drops — whose payload names the decode failure, so the chain rendering is asserted rather than assumed. The eight tripwires acceptance lists do NOT pin it (see there).

The terminal placement over the same broken harness stays hard: it still renders the failure and still exits non-zero. The SARIF arm is NOT here — its home is tests/reporters.rs, beside the template it copies; see that item. The fix must not soften a hard placement while it un-silences the advisory one.

The one out-of-fence assertion the fix inverts. `a_lock_carrying_two_requirement_rows_with_the_same_name_refuses_loud` (:534) asserts `findings.is_empty()` with the comment "a fatal duplicate key error produces no findings (the check exits before collecting them)" — it PINS the bug this entry removes. edit.description: New well-formedness check beside nested_member_admissibility (~60-79, the real neighbor — not satisfies_label_admissibility, which judges a different, host-blind ambiguity): a single host declaring the SAME (kind, key) nested member twice is a malformed lock, refused at admissibility. Two DIFFERENT hosts sharing a (kind, key) are NOT coincident under 0049's grammar (`spec:alpha/invariant/x` and `spec:beta/invariant/x` are distinct addresses) — that case is a resolution-time ambiguity, not an admissibility refusal; see graph.rs below.

`member_named` (:1650) is the ONE membership lookup `resolves` (:1632), `edge_resolves` (:1380) and `member_at` (:466) all read since ab500f80 consolidated them, and its own doc comment (:1646-1649) already names this entry's ruling as owed: a bare key `also names an embedded member, taking whichever member of the kind carries it first ... refusing it is a policy decision owned elsewhere`. Decide it here. Because ab500f80 also made an embedded member's identity ITS ADDRESS (`compose::embedded_member_features`, :1201, `id: graph::nested_address(...)` at :1214), the host is read straight off `features.id` via `parse_nested_address` — no plumbing, no carrier to thread. When a BARE (unqualified) key matches more than one nested member of a kind across different hosts, refuse naming every colliding host; the full host-qualified address always resolves. The refusal cannot be produced AT the lookup — `member_named` returns `Option<&Features>` and `resolves` returns `bool`, neither of which can carry a diagnostic — so it is raised where the dangling diagnostics are already built (the `resolved_edges`/dangling path, and `edge_resolves` for the mention family), as a `graph.route` finding. `by_kind`'s pooled per-kind Vec (`compose::embedded_features_by_kind`, :1139) is what pools the candidates a bare key sees.

`explain`'s bare-name resolution needs the same ambiguity refusal, naming every host the name could mean — and the site is `resolve` (:209), NOT `why_impl` (:832). `resolve` matches by equality (`f.id == name` at :242 for the `kind:name` form, `f.id == target` at :255 for the bare form); since ab500f80 an embedded member's `features.id` is its full nested address, so a bare nested key resolves to NOTHING in explain today — there is no first-match collapse to convert, and the work is an ADDITION at `resolve`: match a bare name against nested members' key segment through the address parser, then refuse naming every host when more than one carries it. (`why_impl`'s dedup at :853 collapses one id borne by several KINDS — a different case `resolve` already refuses as `Species::Ambiguous` at :269-274; leave it alone.) This is what 0049 requires of `explain`: a bare name resolves exactly as an edge's bare identity does, within one declared kind when unique, refused as ambiguous otherwise.

`embedded_hosts_by_source` (:622) is the last partial implementation of "which host owns this nested member": it builds a `(kind, key) -> host` BTreeMap off nested_member rows with a plain `.insert()` (:628), so a cross-host duplicate silently keeps whichever row inserts last, feeding `mention_reachable`'s citation scoping (doc at :615-621). Give it the same ambiguity judgment rather than a third lookup with a third failure mode (engineering.md, "One job, one home"). It also hand-parses the host address at :627 (`row.host.split_once(':')`) — and there is NO host-address parser anywhere in the tree to point it at: `graph::parse_nested_address` demands three slash-separated segments and returns `None` on a bare two-segment `kind:name`, and `extract::host_address` is a writer only. So either read the host off the member's own `features.id` (ab500f80 put it there) and stop parsing `row.host` here at all — preferred — or add the reader half beside the writer. Do not claim `parse_nested_address` already owns this grammar. The full hand-parse inventory, for the record and for MEMBER-ADDRESS-GRAMMAR-ONE-HOME to inherit, is EIGHT sites, all re-verified at 6b9eacae: gate.rs:627, graph.rs:333, :1348, :1624, :1703, read.rs:238, :1994, drift.rs:892. Three corrections to the five an earlier cut listed: drift.rs:891-893 does not split a different string — it splits a host address into (host_kind, host_name) and its refusal names the `kind:name` grammar verbatim; graph.rs:1703 (the host-segment split INSIDE `parse_nested_address`) is the site that literally becomes the reader half; and read.rs:1994 (`prose_strand`, taking the name segment off a `LayoutProseRow.member`) is an eighth. This entry rewrites only gate.rs:627; the other seven are MEMBER-ADDRESS's, whose files[] now carries them.

Three regressions: (1) one host declaring the same (kind, key) nested member twice refuses at admissibility; (2) two different hosts each declaring a same-kind-same-key nested member: a bare/explain-name reference to that key refuses at resolution naming both hosts, while either host's full `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` address always resolves; (3) the same cross-host duplicate reaching `embedded_hosts_by_source` (a body-carried edge citation scoped through it) is judged the same way, not silently mapped to whichever host inserted last. PLUS one existing arm this entry inverts, in-fence and easy to miss: `host_qualified_addresses::a_bare_key_still_names_an_embedded_member` (:886) asserts the bare key `common` resolves with no dangling, over a fixture (`declarations()`, :779-802) that deliberately carries `domain_row("service:alpha", "common")` and `domain_row("service:beta", "common")` — a cross-host duplicate, so its verdict flips to the refusal. Its own comment at :776-778 ("the same key twice, which is the whole point of addressing by host") stays true; the sentence that must change is the one claiming the short form still resolves.

The one out-of-fence test that pins the prior policy this entry overturns: `embedded_edge_targets::a_bare_nested_member_address_matches_first_same_key` (:1188, in tests/graph.rs) builds two `service` hosts each declaring a `domain` member keyed `common`, spells the bare `common` on an edge, and asserts `run.ok` because "bare nested member addresses should resolve to the first match (ambiguous but deterministic)". That IS the codified ambiguity `graph::member_named`'s doc calls "a policy decision owned elsewhere", so deciding it necessarily rewrites this test — into the refusal naming both carrier hosts, or into a host-qualified spelling that still resolves. Same corpus, inverted verdict; keep the case.

VERIFY-ONLY compile guard, expect no diff: :470 binds `graph::resolved_edges(&edges, &by_kind)` and :474 `graph::acyclic(resolved_edges)`, so the ambiguity judgment must need no new parameter on either — its candidate pool IS `by_kind` (`compose::embedded_features_by_kind`) and each embedded member's host rides its own `features.id`. In the fence so a forced signature change lands visibly here rather than failing the fence at the merge.

summary: A duplicate (kind, key) nested member is coincident only within one host; across hosts a bare address is ambiguous at resolution, never silently picked.

tests.asserts: same-host duplicate (kind, key) refuses at admissibility; cross-host duplicate (kind, key) refuses only a bare/unqualified reference, at resolution, naming both hosts, across every bare-key consumer (graph::resolves, explain's `resolve`, src/read.rs:209, embedded_hosts_by_source) — and tests/graph.rs's bare-key edge case is re-pinned to the same verdict
a bare nested-member address matching two hosts refuses at resolution naming both, where the suite previously asserted first-match-wins; the host-qualified spelling of either still resolves

acceptance: A host repeating its own (kind, key) nested member refuses loud at admissibility. Two different hosts sharing a (kind, key) are legal (distinct addresses per 0049); a bare or explain-name reference ambiguous between them refuses at resolution naming every host, while the full host-qualified address to either always resolves. The refusal matches the SDK's, which SHIPPED this same bar at c60ddd3f (sdk/src/emit.ts:340-347: names every carrier host and points at the whole `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` spelling) — one verdict at both ends of the seam, not two wordings. The bar fires at every consumer of a bare key, not only graph::member_named: explain's `resolve` and embedded_hosts_by_source (gate.rs) each name every candidate host too. The regression pins non-vacuity: each case asserts at least one real colliding pair is judged, not an empty read short-circuiting to 'no ambiguity' (0048's conservation bar).

edit.description: `committed_layout_sites` (:54) collects discovered committed members of LAYOUT-content kinds only (the `Content::Layout` filter at :67, the `commitment != Local` exclusion at :68), so 676467cf's undeclared-member finding never sees a composed kind. Generalize it to one site walk over every discovered kind, tagging each site with its content class. ONE predicate, spelled once: `content == Content::File && governs.is_some() && commitment != Local`. Each conjunct is load-bearing — the `local` exclusion is already there, `governs == None` drops a nested-file child (it composes its path from its host and holds no rollup row), and the content class drops the four registration kinds. Those four (hook, installed-plugin, known-marketplace, mcp-server) fall out on the content test ALONE: each is `Content::Fields` carrying a `collection_address` (src/builtin_kind.rs:347, :378, :418, :462), its lock residue `[[declaration.registration]]` and never a provenance row, so joining them would forge false findings over the gauntlet and move the snapshot this entry forbids moving. Do NOT add a `collection_address.is_none()` exclusion beside the content test: the two are not the same predicate (a `Content::Fields` kind with no collection address passes one and fails the other), and a second spelling of one rule is the disease. If a `Content::File` kind carrying a `collection_address` proves admissible, keep it excluded and say why in the commit body rather than widening the predicate silently. Keep the layout branch's rule id and message byte-identical so tests/layout_kind.rs stays green untouched. Gate the whole check on lock presence — on an unrepresented harness every discovered member is undeclared and the finding must stay silent; the layout branch inherits that gate too (it is vacuously safe there today, since layout kinds exist only via lock rows, but it is genuinely load-bearing for file-locus built-ins). Unlike the guard (GUARD-UNDECLARED-LOCUS-WRITE excludes a `.`-rooted locus for want of an ignore reader), `check` KEEPS `.`-rooted loci — `memory` governs `.` with `**/CLAUDE.md` — on purpose: discovery already prunes by the repo's ignore rules (src/import.rs:321-335), so the walk judged is the walk made. Name that deliberate divergence in the commit body. Thread the undeclared set into `coverage_note::check` (:544) — which means MOVING the site walk above that call, from its current home at :563-570.

Beside `undeclared_layout_members_from_doc` (:2820): the composed-kind counterpart. A composed member's whole trace on the lock is its projection provenance row, not the five `MEMBER_ADDRESS_COLUMNS` (:2764) declaration families a layout host reaches through — so this one joins each discovered site's `source_path` against `read_prior_provenance_from_doc` (:2272), the same rows `emit_owned_targets` (:3268) and `config_stale` (:2713) already walk. Normalize BOTH sides through `normalize_lock_path` (:806) before comparing, exactly as the emit reap-diff does at :1417: the site's path is a `String` from `path::relativize_against_root` (gate.rs:74-77) while `ProvenanceRow.source_path` (:2240) is a `HarnessRelativePath`, and an older lock's `./x` spelling would otherwise forge a finding. A discovered document at a represented kind's locus that no provenance row names is reported `locus.undeclared-member` at `warn`, naming path and kind: `emit` will never maintain it (orphan classification iterates lock rows at :1416, so a disk file with no row is never classified and no orphan-drift is reported over it) and `guard` never bound it, yet Claude Code loads it. Remedy named first is declare the member and re-emit. The `local` remedy is offered only for a CUSTOM kind — a built-in cannot be re-declared until BUILTIN-KIND-RELOCATION-EDGE-FIELDS lands. That the sibling layout message at :2832 offers `local` unconditionally is deliberate, not an inconsistency to fix here: no built-in kind carries `Content::Layout` (it arrives only from a lock row), so every layout kind is one whose commitment the author can respell. Say that in the commit body; tests/layout_kind.rs:715's `local` assertion does not move.

`check` (:57) renders `coverage.checked` (:28) from `member_counts` alone, so a stranger document at a governed locus inflates a kind's count with no mark — the observed 11 -> 13. Take the undeclared set gate.rs now computes and disclose declared and undeclared apart per kind, so the one line that says what was checked cannot silently absorb a member the program does not declare. Hard constraint: the line stays BYTE-IDENTICAL when a kind has zero undeclared members — `tests/snapshots/gauntlet__check_diagnostics.snap:7` pins the whole rendering and `tests/gate_fail_loud.rs:228` asserts the `skill (1)` substring (that fixture writes no lock, so the lock-presence gate keeps it green regardless), so the undeclared mark appends only where there is one.

The fixtures here already build harness dirs with a committed lock and read findings back off the GitHub reporter's one-line-per-finding form (`write_skill`, `lock_widget_kind`, `check_harness`), which is exactly this entry's shape. Three new regressions per tests[], plus TWO existing arms that gain an undeclared mark because their own fixtures carry an undeclared document: `an_embedded_kind_with_nested_members_renders_a_nonzero_embedded_marked_count` (:378), whose `assert!(summary.contains("skill (1)"))` at :410 fails once the summary gains the mark, and `a_locked_custom_kind_suppresses_the_surface_it_governs` (:335), which gains an advisory finding its existing assertions survive but which must be pinned rather than left implicit.

`coverage_note::check` is called directly here at :388 with five arguments; threading the undeclared set through it is a compile error in this file until the call is updated. No behavioural claim of this suite changes — it pins cost, not findings.

The gauntlet corpus's whole `coverage.checked` rendering is pinned here (:7). Its members are all declared, so the disclosure change must leave this snapshot unmoved — it is in the fence so a genuine, justified move can be accepted rather than reverting the tick on the fence, not as licence to reformat the line.

summary: A document dropped at a represented kind's locus that the lock declares no member for is admitted, counted, and never named — the file-locus half of 676467cf.

tests.asserts: an undeclared `.claude/rules/*.md` in a represented harness yields one `locus.undeclared-member` warn naming its path and kind, and the `coverage.checked` disclosure counts it apart from the declared members of that kind

the same harness with that document declared and emitted reports neither the finding nor an undeclared count — and asserts a non-zero declared count first, so the silence is not an empty read (0048's conservation bar)
an unrepresented harness (no lock) checked under the built-in default contract reports no `locus.undeclared-member` at all, however many documents discovery finds
